newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes ease amid oversupply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes ease amid oversupply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes eased Monday in thin trade, as refiners scrambled to sell-off a month's worth of extra inventories, traders said.
The excess followed Tosco Corp decision to turn back 40,000 barrels-per-day of February heavy crude, traders said.
The heavy crude was slated to run through Tosco's Avon, Calif., refinery until a fire late last month cut intake.
The cancellations and planned outages at several California refiners have dropped postings in recent weeks, with Mobil and Chevron cutting their offers another 50 cents on Friday.

Texaco, owner of the largest number of turned-back barrels, applied for an emergency crude exporting permit, traders said. The company owns about 30,000 of 40,000 bpd of the cancelled supplies, traders said.
Prices for Kern River heavy grade ranged $17 to 17.25 a barrel on Monday.
Meanwhile, crude traders shrugged off a weekend explosion at Paramount's Los Angeles refinery, noting the plant -- at a 46,000 bpd capacity -- was too small to impact crude supplies.

In light crude markets, Alaskan grade bids eased five cents in line with weaker West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude. The March crude contract, the basis for Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude, dipped on the heels of lower heating oil futures.
Outright ANS prices were $22.65/22.85 a barrel, with the differential holding at $1.45 under WTI.
BP, the grade's dominant producer, offered crude at $1.25 under WTI, while the best bid was $2.00 a barrel under March WTI.
